sling = a cloth that holds an injured arm against the body
stitches = thread used to close a deep cut
plaster cast = a hard covering that keeps a broken bone still
ice pack = a cold bag you put on a swelling
thermometer = an instrument that measures body temperature
stethoscope = the instrument a doctor uses to listen to your heart and lungs
waiting list = a list of people who must wait for treatment
specialist = a doctor who knows a lot about one part of the body
optometrist = a person who tests your eyesight
glasses = lenses in a frame that help you see better
contact lenses = small lenses you put on your eyes instead of glasses
hearing aid = a small device that helps you hear
disabled = having a condition that makes some activities harder
disabled toilet = a larger toilet with extra space and support
mental health = how well your mind and feelings are
stress = worry and pressure that can make you feel ill
anxious = worried and nervous, often for a long time
depressed = very sad for a long time and unable to enjoy things
insomnia = when you cannot sleep well for many nights
exhausted = extremely tired
